messages:
support-elaine: Hey team — escalating a customer p99 latency spike after we onboarded vortex-2 yesterday. Customer reports large context generations (12k+ tokens) seeing p99 from ~450ms -> ~2.6s. They pasted a couple of requests and the endpoint: POST /v1/generate model=vortex-2-1.0. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.example.com/r/1234 (perf graphs attached). They're high-volume and it's impacting SLAs :frowning_face:

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2023-17654 — p99 latency increase observed for model vortex-2 across long-context buckets (>8k tokens). Initial severity: Sev2. Autoinvestigation started.

devex-ryan: thanks @support-elaine. can you paste a minimal repro curl and exact payload sizes? also which variant (vortex-2-1.0 vs vortex-2-quant) are affected?

support-elaine: repro below (sanitized). Affected: vortex-2-1.0 (hosted), we see similar but less severe on vortex-2-quant.

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"vortex-2-1.0","input":"<long prompt with ~12k tokens>","max_tokens":512}'

Context: original prompt is system + ~10 user messages (~12k tokens). On smaller prompts (<2k) latency is normal.

ml-onboard-jin: ping — I was the eng who rolled the vortex-2 tokenizer update. We switched tokenizer from bpe-v1 to bpe-v2 during onboarding to improve OOV handling. I've compared tokenization for the sample prompt:

```
# sample diffs
old (bpe-v1) tokens: 10124
new (bpe-v2) tokens: 12597
# bpe-v2 splits many CJK and punctuation sequences differently -> substantially longer sequences
```

This increases KV cache footprint and unexpectedly pushes requests into a different execution path (degraded attention kernel chosen for long sequences). I suspect the runtime kernel selection threshold is being hit more frequently now.

infra-oliver: I pulled runtime logs from runtime-serving-8 for the timestamp range. Evidence of cache churn and repeated kv-cache-map misses around request start:

```
2024-06-12T18:24:01Z runtime-serving-8 WARNING kv_cache: shard_miss shard=23 key=0x9f12a...
2024-06-12T18:24:01Z runtime-serving-8 INFO  batch_scheduler: started batch id=6789 size=1 expected_latency=2.3s
2024-06-12T18:24:02Z runtime-serving-8 ERROR attention: fallback to slow-attn kernel seq_len=8192 token_len=12597
```

We don't usually see that many slow-attn fallbacks for this model. Also memory pressure metrics spiked on worker nodes serving vortex-2.

oncall-aj: suggested quick mitigations: 1) route long-context traffic to vortex-2-compat (a compatibility variant that uses bpe-v1) 2) set a temporary policy to cap max_input_tokens to 8192 for hosted tier customers 3) pause the tokenizer rollout and rollback to bpe-v1 for vortex-2 globally if needed. Which should we try first?

devex-ryan: let's avoid global rollback if possible. Can infra do a routing rule to divert 10% of traffic to vortex-2-compat for the affected customers and compare p99? If that shows improvement, we can ramp. Also support, please ask the customer if they can accept the 8192 cap as a short-term workaround.

sre-ops-liz: I'll run the canary routing now. Steps: 1) create route policy rule "compat-canary-10pct" 2) apply to customer tag customer:acme-inc 3) monitor p99 for 15m. Running command:

redwood routing create --name compat-canary-10pct --match "customer:acme-inc" --actions "model:vortex-2-compat,weight:10"

sre-ops-liz: Applied at 2024-06-12T18:40:12Z. Monitoring...

support-elaine: Customer updated: they're willing to accept the 8k cap for 48hrs while we investigate. For enterprise tier they requested ETA before we change their traffic.

infra-oliver: early results from the canary: p99 for diverted 10% dropped back to ~480ms, mainline stays ~2.5s. So tokenizer difference is strongly correlated.

ml-onboard-jin: Good — this confirms tokenizer change is the main factor. Short-term fix options: A) revert tokenizer to bpe-v1 mapping for vortex-2 B) regenerate bpe-v2 merges to preserve average tokenization length for long-context workloads (we did naive training on web corpus, not heavy long-doc corpora) C) tweak kernel-selection thresholds in the serving runtime to avoid slow-attn for seq_len up to 13k (but that risks more memory).

I ran a small test where we retokenized 20 sample long prompts with an adjusted merges table; p99 decode time reduced ~40% vs current bpe-v2 and token counts fell to ~11.5k. Will create repro artifacts.

infra-oliver: Note: changing kernel thresholds requires release and may take ~2 days to validate. Regenerating merges might be fastest but we need to validate semantics (no regression in quality).

oncall-aj: Action summary so far: 1) canary routing applied (sre-ops-liz) 2) customer agreed to 8k cap (support-elaine) 3) ml will produce regen-merge candidate and perf QA (ml-onboard-jin) 4) infra to add tokenization-length variance metric & alert (infra-oliver). Can we get owners and SLAs for each item?

ml-onboard-jin: Owner: ml-onboard-jin — will deliver regen candidate + evaluation by EOD 2024-06-13. QA run will include perf and quality regression checks (ROUGE/BLEU and a small human pass).

infra-oliver: Owner: infra-oliver — add histogram metric token_len_per_request and alert if p99 token_len growth > 15% vs baseline. ETA: 2024-06-14 morning.

sre-ops-liz: Owner: sre-ops-liz — monitor canary for 6h and if stable ramp to 50% then 100%. Will rollback routing if errors > 0.5% or p50 degradation.

support-elaine: I'll send a customer-facing note summarizing the workaround and ETA.

devex-ryan: follow-up: please add the exact reproduction requests to the incident ticket and include the small diff script that shows token counts for old vs new tokenizers. Also collect a sample of requests that triggered slow-attn fallback so runtime team can reproduce locally.

ml-onboard-jin: uploaded tokenization diff script and sample prompts to the incident artifacts bundle: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2023-17654/artifacts.tar.gz. Script output example:

```
> python3 token_diff.py sample1.txt
old_tokens=10124 new_tokens=12597 delta=2463
```

infra-oliver: added a temporary dashboard panel to the model perf page showing "token_len distribution by model variant" and wired a Grafana alert.

oncall-aj: thanks everyone. Next steps: ml will push a regen candidate; infra will validate metrics/alerts; support will keep customer informed and maintain 8k cap. We'll reconvene in 6 hours or earlier if canary shows ramp issues. Closing thread when all owners confirm. :thumbsup:

support-elaine: Notifying customer now. Will post updates here. Thanks all :pray:
